title: Muslims disproportionately flagged in Delhi SIR
shows: The Hindu read Delhi's draft roll of 97.54 lakh electors, matched it to the lists of the 33.12 lakh sent notices (13.79 lakh unmapped with the last SIR and 19.33 lakh for logical discrepancies), and guessed each elector's religion from their name and their relative's name. On that guess, Muslims were 13.6% of the draft roll, 7.6% of the unmapped and 20.3% of those flagged for logical discrepancies, and 30% of those flagged for the five reasons that turn on family size, such as six or more electors naming the same parent. The paper reports that ERONET, the Commission's software, decided who was flagged, that the reasons appear in no SIR order before the direction of 14 May 2026, and that the Commission had not answered its questions.
quote: Muslims, who form 13.6% of electors on Delhi’s draft roll, made up 20.3% of those flagged for “logical discrepancies”, and 30% of those flagged under five reasons indicative of family size.
The Hindu digitised Delhi’s draft SIR rolls, which had 97.54 lakh voters, of whom 33.12 lakh were flagged for notices by the ECI
13.79 lakh were flagged for being “Unmapped with Last SIR” and another 19.33 lakh for “logical discrepancies” based on eight reasons.
Among the 13.79 lakh who were “Unmapped with Last SIR,” members of the community accounted for only 7.6%
Of the 6.75 lakh electors who were flagged for one or more of these reasons, 30% were Muslims
the decision on who would be flagged was not theirs, but decided by the centralised ERONET software
The issue of notices to electors for “discrepancies” found a mention for the first time only in ECI’s direction issued on May 14, 2026
To estimate religion, we used an open-source classifier built by Rochana Chaturvedi and Sugat Chaturvedi (Political Analysis, 2023).
The ECI did not respond till Tuesday night.
